transcript: I was a little nervous about Floyd Collins after hearing some conflicting thoughts from folks who attended earlier previews, but I actually ended up loving it. Currently running at Lincoln Center, this is a musical about a cave explorer who becomes trapped underground. Most of the show follows the efforts made in the attempt to rescue him, the toll this takes on his family, and how the story captures public attention, resulting in a media circus. This isn't a story I think I'd normally be drawn to, but Jeremy Jordan in the title role was more than enough to get me excited about it. Across the board, I thought the vocal performances were amazing — obviously Jeremy Jordan but also Jason Gotay and Lizzy McAlpine who play Floyd’s siblings. This marks Lizzy's Broadway debut, and she wasn't quite as natural on stage as some of the other actors, but I still thought she did a good job and her voice is so perfect for this folky score by Adam Guettel. I really want a cast recording or at least a professional recording of her singing “Through the Mountain.” Overall, the singing and the score were really what made the show for me, and I can testify that any sound design or mixing issues that I heard were problematic early in the run have since been resolved. And thankfully so, as it's not an otherwise riveting musical. For a show where the only things that really happen are a man getting stuck in a cave and people trying to get him out, it's too long, with book scenes that are only semi-related to the songs they surround. I didn't find it boring per se, but it all could have been more concise. I also didn't find the staging of this production very interesting, but I won't harp on this since it is a weird show that seems like it would be hard to stage in general. I enjoyed the lighting design a lot though, and while I don't think this show is for everyone, the score and these performances had me totally locked in. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
